ny);\n    const double* __restrict ryp = c + idx3(0, yp, z, nx, ny);\n    const double* __restrict ryn = c + idx3(0, yn, z, nx, ny);\n    const double* __restrict rzp = c + idx3(0, y, zp, nx, ny);\n    const double* __restrict rzn = c + idx3(0, y, zn, nx, ny);\n    double* __restrict out = mu + idx3(0, y, z, nx, ny);\n\n    auto point = [&](const size_t x, const size_t xp, const size_t xn) {\n        const double cv = r[x];\n        out[x] = 4.5 * ((cv + 1.0) * e_AA + (cv - 1.0) * e_BB - 2.0 * cv * e_AB)\n                 + 3.0 * cv + cv * cv * cv\n                 - gamma * laplacianPoint(r[xp], r[xn], ryp[x], ryn[x], rzp[x], rzn[x], cv, dx2, dy2, dz2);\n    };\n\n    if (nx == 1) {\n        point(0, 0, 0);\n        return;\n    }\n    point(0, 1, 0);\n#pragma omp simd\n x-row (fixed y, z) with clamped boundary conditions\nstatic inline void cahnHilliardRow(double* __restrict cnew, const double* __restrict cold,\n                                   const double* }\n\n    // Run simulation\n    printf(\"Running Cahn-Hilliard simulation...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    // Reference divides by (dx*dx) etc.; keep x < nx - 1; ++x) {\n        const double cv = r[x];\n        out[x] = 4.5 * ((cv + 1.0) * e_AA + (cv - 1.0) * e_BB - 2.0 * cv * e_AB)\n                 + 3.0 * cv + cv * cv * cv\n                 - gamma * laplacianPoint(r[x + 1], r[x - 1], ryp[x], ryn[x], rzp[x], rzn[x], cv, dx2, dy2, dz2);\n    }\n    point(nx - 1, nx - 1, nx - 2);\n}\n\n// Cahn-Hilliard update for one x-row with clamped boundary conditions.\n// m is the mu row itself; myp/myn/mzp/mzn are the (already clamped) neighbouring mu rows.\nstatic inline void cahnHilliardRow(double* __restrict out, const double* __restrict co,\n                                   const double* __restrict m,\n                                   const double* __restrict myp, const double* __restrict myn,\n                                   const double* __restrict mzp, const double* __restrict mzn,\n                                   const size_t nx, const Params& p) noexcept {\n    const double dx2 = p.dx2, dy2 = p.dy2, dz2 = p.dz2;\n    const double D = p.D, dt = p.dt;\n\n    auto point = [&](const size_t x, const size_t xp, const size_t xn) {\n        out[x] = co[x] + dt * D *\n                 laplacianPoint(m[xp], m[xn], myp[x], myn[x], mzp[x], mzn[x], m[x], dx2, dy2, dz2);\n    };\n\n    if (nx == 1) {\n        point(0, 0, 0);\n        return;\n    }\n    point(0, 1, 0);\n#pragma omp simd\n    for (size_t x = 1; x < nx - 1; ++x) {\n        out[x] = co[x] + dt * D *\n                 laplacianPoint(m[x + 1], m[x - 1], myp[x], myn[x], mzp[x], mzn[x], m[x], dx2, dy2, dz2);\n    }\n    point(nx - 1, nx - 1, nx - 2);\n}\n\n// Static 2D (z, y) tile decomposition: each thread owns one tile for the whole run, so\n// pages first-touched during initialization stay local to the thread that uses them.\nstruct Tile {\n    size_t z0, z1, y0, y1; a <= std::min(nthreads, nz); ++a) {\n        const size_t b = std::min(nthreads / a, ny);\n        if (b == 0) continue;\n        const size_t used = a * b;\n        const double tz = static_cast<double>(nz) / a;\n        const double ty = static_cast<double>(ny) / b;\n        const double cost = 2.0 / tz + 2.0 / ty;\n        if (used > bestUsed || (used == bestUsed && cost < bestCost)) {\n            bestUsed = used;\n            bestCost = cost;\n            pz = a;\n            py = b;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nstatic Tile tileFor(const size_t tid, const size_t pz, const size_t py, const size_t ny, const size_t nz) {\n    if (tid >= pz * py) return Tile{0, 0, 0, 0};\n    const size_t iz = tid / py;\n    const size_t iy = tid % py;\n    auto lo = [](size_t n, size_t parts, size_t i) { return (n / parts) * i + std::min(i, n % parts); halo values are simply\n// recomputed redundantly by neighbouring tiles.\nstatic void fusedStepTile(double* __restrict cnew, const double* __restrict cold, double* __restrict win,\n                          const Tile& t, const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz, const Params& p) {\n    if (t.z0 >= t.z1 || t.y0 >= t.y1) return;\n\n    const size_t ya = (t.y0 > 0) ? t.y0 - 1 : 0;           // first mu row needed\n    const size_t yb = (t.y1 < ny) ? t.y1 : ny - 1;         // last mu row needed (inclusive)\n    const size_t rows = yb - ya + 1;\n    const size_t planeStride = rows * nx;\n\n    auto slot = [&](size_t zz) -> double* { return win + (zz % 3) * planeStride; };\n    auto muRow = [&](size_t zz, size_t y) -> const double* { return slot(zz) + (y - ya) * nx; };\n\n    auto computeMuPlane = [&](size_t zz) {\n        const size_t zp = (zz < nz - 1) ? zz + 1 : zz;\n        const size_t zn = (zz > 0) ? zz - 1 : 0;\n        double* dst = slot(zz);\n        for (size_t y = ya; y <= yb; ++y) {\n            const size_t yp = (y < ny - 1) ? y + 1 : y;\n            const size_t yn = (y > 0) ? y - 1 : 0;\n            chemicalPotentialRow(dst + (y - ya) * nx,\n                                 cold + idx3(0, y, zz, nx, ny),\n                                 cold + idx3(0, yp, zz, nx, ny),\n                                 cold + idx3(0, yn, zz, nx, ny),\n                                 cold + idx3(0, y, zp, nx, ny),\n                                 cold + idx3(0, y, zn, nx, ny),\n                                 nx, p);\n        }\n    };\n\n    // Prime the window with planes z0-1 (clamped) and z0\n    size_t nextMu = (t.z0 > 0) ? t.z0 - 1 : 0;\n    const size_t lastMu = (t.z1 < nz) ? t.z1 : nz - 1;  // inclusive\n\n    for (size_t z = t.z0; z < t.z1; ++z) {\n        const size_t zp = (z < nz - 1) ? z + 1 : z;\n        const size_t zn = (z > 0) ? z - 1 : 0;\n        while (nextMu <= zp && nextMu <= lastMu) {\n            computeMuPlane(nextMu);\n            ++nextMu;\n        }\n        for (size_t y = t.y0; Evaluation order matches the\n// reference formulation exactly. With Recip == true the divisors are replaced by their\n// reciprocals, which is only used when those are exact (powers of two), so results are\n// bitwise identical to dividing.\ntemplate <bool Recip>\nstatic inline double laplacianPoint(const double xp, const double xn, const double yp, const double yn,\n                                    const double zp, const double zn, const double cc,\n                                    const double sx, const double sy, const double sz) noexcept {\n    double cxx, cyy, czz;\n    if constexpr (Recip) {\n        cxx = (xp + xn - 2.0 * cc) * sx;\n        cyy = (yp + yn - 2.0 * cc) * sy;\n        czz = (zp + zn - 2.0 * cc) * sz;\n    } else {\n        cxx = (xp + xn - 2.0 * cc) / sx;\n        cyy = (yp + yn - 2.0 * cc) / sy;\n        czz = (zp + zn - 2.0 * cc) / sz;\n    }\n    return cxx + cyy + czz;\n}\n\n// True if 1/v is exactly representable (v is a normal power of two)\nstatic bool hasExactReciprocal(const double v) {\n    int e = 0;\n    return std::isnormal(v) && std::frexp(v, &e) == 0.5 && std::isnormal(1.0 / v);\n}\n\n'''\ns=s.replace(old_lap,new_lap)\ns=s.replace('''struct Params {\n    double dx2, dy2, dz2;''','''struct Params {\n    double sx, sy, sz;  // dx^2, dy^2, dz^2 or their exact reciprocals (see laplacianPoint)''')\ns=s.replace('const double dx2 = p.dx2, dy2 = p.dy2, dz2 = p.dz2;','const double dx2 = p.sx, dy2 = p.sy, dz2 = p.sz;')\ns=s.replace('laplacianPoint(','laplacianPoint<Recip>(').replace('static inline double laplacianPoint<Recip>(','static inline double laplacianPoint(')\nfor f in ['static inline void chemicalPotentialRow','static inline void cahnHilliardRow','static void fusedStepTile']:\n    s=s.replace(f,'template <bool Recip>\\n'+f)\ns=s.replace('chemicalPotentialRow(dst','chemicalPotentialRow<Recip>(dst').replace('cahnHilliardRow(cnew','cahnHilliardRow<Recip>(cnew')\ns=s.replace('''    // Reference divides by (dx*dx) etc.; keep identical arithmetic\n    const Params params{dx * dx, dy * dy, dz * dz, gamma, e_AA, e_BB, e_AB, D, dt};''','''    // Reference divides by (dx*dx) etc.; multiply by the reciprocal only when that is exact\n    const bool useRecip = hasExactReciprocal(dx * dx) && hasExactReciprocal(dy * dy) && hasExactReciprocal(dz * dz);\n    const Params params = useRecip\n        ? Params{1.0 / (dx * dx), 1.0 / (dy * dy), 1.0 / (dz * dz), gamma, e_AA, e_BB, e_AB, D, dt}\n        : Params{dx * dx, dy * dy, dz * dz, gamma, e_AA, e_BB, e_AB, D, dt};''')\ns=s.replace('''            fusedStepTile(cnew, cold, window.data(), tile, nx, ny, nz, params);''','''            if (useRecip) {\n                fusedStepTile<true>(cnew, cold, window.data(), tile, nx, ny, nz, params);\n            } else {\n                fusedStepTile<false>(cnew, cold, window.data(), tile, nx, ny, nz, params);\n            }''')\nopen(p,'w').write(s)\nEOF\ncmake --build /tmp/chb 2>&1 | grep -E 'warn|error|Built'; B=/tmp/chb/cahn_hilliard; OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 $B -x 256 -i 20 -r | grep -E 'time|Hash'; for s in 256 512; do for n in 64 128 256; do echo \"$s n=$n $(OMP_NUM_THREADS=$n $B -x $s -i 20 | grep time)\"; done; done"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":424,"cache_read_input_tokens":42396,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":424},"output_tokens":7,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"6fdbc264-ba03-42a2-9fae-7df907f33356","uuid":"ccc50427-d6ed-4f2e-8438-ca454d2e1caf","timestamp":"2026-10-03T07:46:14.040Z","request_id":"req_011Cfew2xzZm8f7qComtAP1b"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfew8AS2Zc8ssTtCfcuqG","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The code in `cahn-hilliard/` now runs in parallel with OpenMP and always uses it. Its output is bit-for-bit identical to the original: the result hash matched on every test case. I tested 9 grid shapes (including 1×1×1 and other degenerate ones), thread counts from 1 to 256, with and without `OMP_PROC_BIND` set. The build has no warnings, `-v` validation passes, and I only changed the two existing files.\n\n**Speed** (2-socket EPYC 7763, 128 cores / 256 threads, 20 steps, timed region only):\n\n| Grid | Original (serial) | OpenMP version |\n|---|---|---|\n| 256³ | ~830–2000 ms | **~17–30 ms** |\n| 512³ | 21,154 ms | **~250 ms** (~85x) |\n\nThe original's 256³ time varied between runs. 256 threads (the default) was slightly slower than 128 at both sizes, so `OMP_NUM_THREADS=128` gives the best numbers on this machine.\n\n**What changed in `cahn_hilliard.cpp`:**\n- **Combined the two passes.** Each thread owns a fixed block of the grid. It works through the block along z and keeps the chemical-potential values in a small private buffer (3 planes) that stays in its cache. This removes the large `mu` array and cuts memory traffic from about 5 array passes per step to about 2. At the edge of each block a thread recomputes a few values its neighbours also compute, using the exact same arithmetic. There is now one barrier per step instead of two.\n- **Memory placement.** The arrays are allocated without being filled, then each thread writes its own block first. On this two-socket machine that puts each block in the memory closest to the thread that uses it.\n- **Thread pinning.** Without pinning, Linux moved threads between cores and sockets, which made the program about 20x slower and made it get slower as threads were added. If you haven't set `OMP_PROC_BIND` or `OMP_PLACES`, each thread now pins itself to one CPU using the standard `sched_setaffinity` call. If you have set them, your settings are used instead.\n- **Divisions.** The inner loops are vectorized. The divisions by dx², dy², dz² become multiplications only when the spacings are powers of two, because only then does that give exactly the same result. Otherwise it still divides.\n- **Allocation moved out of the timer.** Per-thread buffers are allocated during initialization, before the timer starts, like the original arrays. Allocating them inside the timed region added about 20 ms to the first step.\n- **Output copy.** The final field is copied into a `std::vector` after the timer stops, so `print_results` and validation work unchanged.\n\n`CMakeLists.txt` now uses `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)` and links `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX`. The executable name is still `cahn_hilliard`."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":831,"cache_read_input_tokens":47138,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":831},"output_tokens":7,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"6fdbc264-ba03-42a2-9fae-7df907f33356","uuid":"d74f8692-d809-4588-b01d-16f0e8c85896","timestamp":"2026-10-03T07:47:19.755Z","request_id":"req_011Cfew8A6BtWbPARGYfy4Eh"}
